rows: The Olney Fire Department reported baseball-size hail.
A tree fell on a transformer knocking out power to about 20,000 people.
Power lines and poles were downed with power outages reported.
An awning at a house on First Street was torn down by thunderstorm winds. Oak trees were split and blown down.
Baseball to golfball-size hail was reported south of Olney.
Hangars were damaged at Olney Airport. Trees, power poles, and fences were blown down along FM 2178, West Payne Street, West Elm Street, and West Main Street.
Trees were uprooted and a carport was damaged.
Golfball-size hail was reported in town.
A 60 MPH wind gust was reported.
Numerous power poles and trees were blown down. Signs were also damaged. In Graham, a carport was blown onto power lines on Alford Street.
Nickel size hail fell in Olney.
Minor roof damage was observed in Newcastle. Shingles were torn off other houses.
Several trees were knocked down across the county.
Nickel size hail was reported in Graham.
Nickel size hail was reported 5 miles east of Graham.
A large oak tree was split in half at Oak Street Baptist Church. Part of the tree fell on the street.
Hail up to the size of a half-dollar fell in the city of Graham.

PSI Industries in Olney lost its roof and a door due to thunderstorm winds. Also in Olney, the drive-thru menu at Dairy Queen was knocked over, the sign at Goldsmith Supply Co. was damaged, and trees, tree limbs, signs, and power poles were knocked down. A possible downburst may …
A heatburst associated with dissipating convection occurred in Young County. The Olney Emergency Manager estimated 60 MPH winds with the heatburst. No damage was reported.
A heatburst associated with dissipating convection occurred in Young County. The fire department in Graham estimated 60 MPH winds with the heatburst. No damage was reported.
Two local businesses were damaged, homes suffered minor damage, and numerous trees were uprooted around Olney.
Nickel sized hail was reported 1 mile east of Graham.
Nickel to quarter sized hail was reported west of Olney.
Ping pong ball sized hail fell 3 miles southeast of Olney.
Golfball sized hail was reported on Highway 114 between Olney and Loving.
Golfball sized hail fell along FM 578 between Newcastle and Murray.
Several sources reported quarter to golfball sized hail in Graham. The local newspaper reported hundreds of homes and vehicles were damaged by the hail.

The roof of a metal garage was blown off by thunderstorm winds in Graham. Power lines were also knocked down. The automated weather station at the airport (KRPH) measured a 47 mph wind gust at the time.
Tennis ball sized hail was reported 2 miles east of Graham.
Sixty MPH winds were estimated to the south of Olney.
Ping pong to golfball sized hail was covering the ground in Eliasville.
Golf ball sized hail was reported in South Bend.
Ping pong to golf ball sized hail was reported in Graham.
Golf ball sized hail was reported east of Woodson near the Throckmorton/Young county line.
Nickel sized hail was reported 6 miles west of Newcastle on FM 926.
Nickel to quarter sized hail was reported in South Olney.
Half dollar sized hail was reported in Newcastle.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported in Newcastle via HAM radio.
Storm spotters estimated thunderstorm winds of 60 mph in Newcastle.
Quarter sized hail was reported 3 miles west of Red Top.
A 2-foot pecan tree was blown down in Olney. Outbuildings and fences were also damaged.
Thunderstorm winds up to 60 MPH were estimated in Olney by the Emergency Manager.
Another wind gust in Olney was estimated to be 60 MPH.
Thunderstorm winds were estimated to be near 60 MPH north of Olney, near the county line.
A 59 MPH wind gust was measured at KRPH.
Tennis to baseball sized hail was reported near Fort Belknap State Park.

Downburst winds caused damage in Newcastle. Large trees were knocked down; some of the trees were a foot in diameter. Power lines and power poles were also knocked down. Light roof damage was reported around the town, and a few 15'x15' outbuilding were blown up against houses.
Penny sized hail was reported about 8 miles north of Graham.
Winds were estimated to be 60 MPH about 6 miles south of Olney.
Two power poles were blown over east of Newcastle along Highway 380.

The Emergency Manager estimated 55-60 MPH winds in Olney. Some damage was reported on the south and southwest side of town around Mockingbird and Thomas Streets. Some trees were uprooted and a few homes had minor roof and porch damage. One carport was also damaged and part of the…
Dime sized hail was reported in Olney.
Power lines, power poles, fences and trees were reported blown down in the city of Olney. Damage to storage buildings, shingles, and broken windows were also reported.
Golf ball sized hail was reported in Newcastle.
Quarter to ping pong ball sized hail fell south of Loving.
Walnut sized hail was covering most of the ground 6 miles south of Megargel.
Golf ball sized hail was reported at the Olney Municipal Airport.
Golf ball sized hail was reported 3.5 miles west-southwest of Olney, near the Olney Municipal Airport.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported 4 miles west-southwest of Olney.
Hail up to the size of quarters was reported along Highway 79 to the southwest of Olney.
Hail up to the size of quarters was reported near Orth and Highway 251 to the south of Olney.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Graham.
Hail increased to the size of baseballs in Graham.
The Olney Emergency Manager reported hail to the size of a baseball within the city.
Trained spotters reported golf ball sized hail on the west side of Graham.
Trained spotters reported ping pong ball sized hail in Graham.
Trained spotters reported hail between nickel and golf ball sized hail with very little rainfall.
Hail to the size of a chicken egg was reported on the southwest side of Graham.
Tennis ball sized hail was reported near Graham.
Hail was reported in Graham. The hail was becoming smaller, but still included anything from the size of a nickel to the size of a golf ball.
An off duty National Weather Service meteorologist reported another round of hail in Graham. The hail was at least the size of a chicken egg.
Hail to the size of a chicken egg was reported near Newcastle. Quarter and golf ball sized hail was also reported.
Hail to the size of a tea cup was reported in Newcastle.
A broadcast media chaser reported hail that measured 3.5 inches in diameter.
Trained spotters observed a tornado outside of Eliasville. This was the first of two tornadoes, and was the largest. However, this tornado occurred over open land, and produced little to no damage.

Trained spotters observed a tornado outside of Eliasville. This was the second of two tornadoes this day. This tornado was very narrow, but produced EF-1 damage to a home. This tornado moved from the northeast to the southwest.
Golfball to tennis ball sized hail was reported to the west of the city of South Bend. The report was made by the South Bend Fire Department.
Emergency management reported trees down with wind gusts up to 60 MPH.
Golf ball sized hail has reported by fire and rescue 6 miles southwest of Newcastle, TX.
Tennis ball sized hail was reported by a member of the broadcast media 3 miles north-northeast of Murray, TX.
Young County Volunteer Fire Departments reported a roof was torn off of a house in Murray.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported 1 mile south of Olney, TX by emergency management.
Young County Sheriff's deputies reported quarter sized hail north of Newcastle.
The Young County Emergency Manager reported golf ball sized hail at Fort Belknap.
Amateur radio spotters reported quarter sized hail.
Nickel to golf ball sized hail was reported in Graham.
The Graham Leader posted that thunderstorm winds uprooted trees, knocked down at least two structures, and damaged power lines.
Quarter sized hail was reported near Graham.
Law enforcement reported that power lines were down near the Young/Stephens County line.
Emergency management reported golf ball sized hail on FM 3109 approximately 8 miles west of Graham, TX.
Emergency management reported golf ball sized hail on FM 3109 approximately 8 miles west of Graham, TX.
A trained spotter observed a tornado northwest of Loving. The tornado occurred in open fields, and produced little to no damage.
A trained spotter observed a second tornado to the northwest of Loving. This tornado also produced minimal damage over open country.
Half dollar sized hail was reported just west of Graham.
Fire and Rescue reported trees and power lines down in Loving, TX.
Two inch diameter hail was reported near the Graham Airport.

A trained spotter reported golf ball sized hail approximately one mile west of Murray, TX.
Fire and rescue reported a wind gust of 60 MPH about a mile west of Murray, TX.
Emergency management reported a 60 MPH wind gust approximately 5 miles west of Olney, TX.
Emergency management reported trees snapped and damage to the roof and carport of a house about a mile south of Olney, TX.
Young County Sheriff's Department reported quarter-sized hail in Graham, TX.
A trained storm spotter reported quarter sized hail 4 miles south-southeast of the city of Olney, TX.
A trained storm spotter reported half-dollar sized hail 2 miles south-southeast of the city of Olney, TX.
Emergency management reported golf-ball sized hail near the city of Olney, TX.
A storm chaser reported quarter-sized hail approximately 4 miles west-southwest of the city of Newcastle, TX.
Young County Sheriff's department reported quarter sized hail in the city of Olney, TX.
Young County Sheriff's Department reported a few trees blown down in Olney.
A trained spotter reported ping pong ball sized hail near the city of Olney, TX.
Graham, TX Fire Department reported dime to penny sized hail in the city of Graham.
Fire and rescue reported that a boat dock became detached and destroyed, shingles were removed from a roof and heavy damage was done to a back porch from thunderstorm winds at Lake Graham.
A social media report indicated golf ball size hail in the city of Olney, TX.
A trained spotter reported ping pong ball size hail approximately one mile north-northeast of the city of Olney, TX.
A social media report indicated golf ball size hail approximately 12 miles north-northeast of the city of Graham, TX.

A severe thunderstorm emerged out of Stephens County, moving into the southern portions of Young County. A tornado developed near the South Bend region, where damage occurred to several homes and businesses. The tornado continued moving northeast, paralleling HWY 67 toward Graham…

The same thunderstorm that produced the tornado near South Bend produced another tornado to the east, just south of Pettus Ln and Old Hwy 16. This storm moved north, mainly causing tree damage. There was one home in the path which sustained minor roof damage. The tornado dissipat…

Thunderstorm winds associated with a tornadic supercell caused damage at the Wildcatter Ranch south of Graham. Part of a metal roof was peeled back on a shed and several trees were damaged, uprooted or snapped.
Thunderstorm winds damaged one home in Graham, peeling back portions of the metal roof.
A trained spotter sent in a picture of approximate baseball sized hail in the Farmer, Texas area in Young County.
Golf ball to baseball sized hail was reported by broadcast media and trained spotters in the city of Loving, TX.
A wind gust of 60 MPH was reported by the Automated Weather Observation System at Graham Airport.
Emergency management reported roof damage to a building near Main Street and trees down near downtown in the city of Olney, TX.
Large hail was measured south of Loving.
A 64 mph wind gust was measured at Graham Municipal Airport.
The local fire department reported golfball sized hail about a mile west of Eliasville, TX along FM 1974.
Dime sized hail reported near Newcastle.
HAM estimated a 60 mph wind gust southeast of Graham.
Two inch hail was reported near Southbend, Tx.
Golf ball sized hail reported 10 miles northwest of Newcastle.
Golf ball sized hail reported near Loving.
Large tree limbs were broken and trees were uprooted west of Graham along Hwy 67 and also in and around Graham. Lightweight metal structures, outbuildings, and roofs were also damaged.
A collapsing thunderstorm produced a small downburst west of Newcastle near Hwy 380 and FM 578 that damaged trees, broke power poles, and blew a car off the road.
A member of the public reported hail up to golf ball about 6 miles south of Graham on Highway 67. The report was relayed by a Ham Radio Operator.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Graham multiple times. One report was from a trained spotter, and another was from a broadcast media partner.
Emergency manager reported golf ball sized hail in Olney.

Broadcast media reported a downed power pole and sheet metal outbuilding blown apart east of Graham on Highway 380. There were also multiple reports of other metal buildings and small structures damaged in and around Graham.
A 71 mph (62 knot) wind gust was measured by the Graham Municipal Airport AWOS.
A person on Facebook reported golf ball sized hail in Loving.

Emergency manager reported a large shipping container that was one quarter full of wood was flipped onto its side and tossed several feet from its original location. A barbed wire fence was pulled up and minor roof damage was done to a home northwest of Bryson.
Broadcast media reported golf ball, tennis ball, and larger than baseball hail SE of Olney.
A photo of half dollar to ping pong ball sized hail located northeast of Graham was received on social media.
Trained spotter reported golf ball sized hail on Furr Rd. northwest of Newcastle.
A storm chaser reported 1 to 1.3 inch hail in Eliasville. The time was estimated by radar.

Scattered downed trees and sheet metal was removed from buildings throughout Olney. Wooden power poles were leaning, spectator stands at the baseball fields were damaged, and a 40 foot storage container was moved.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail 5 and 1/2 miles north of Lake Graham.
